item.title: Microsoft AI package hijacked, NGINX flaw, PHP patch due Thursday
item.description:
A Microsoft agent framework package on PyPI was hijacked to steal credentials, and a ten-year-old NGINX flaw can allow code execution. PHP has another critical release due Thursday, and F5 disclosed six critical BIG-IP flaws. Also covered are Gemini 4 Neon, banks shifting AI agent risk to customers, and an Irish credit union data breach.

Stories covered:

  • Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI package compromised — Sources: BleepingComputer, The Register Security
  • Decade-old NGINX HTTP/2 flaw allows remote code execution — Sources: The Hacker News, The Register Security, SANS Internet Storm Center
  • Another critical PHP security release due Thursday — Sources: The Register Security
  • F5 discloses six critical BIG-IP flaws — Sources: The Hacker News
  • Gemini 4 Neon rolls out, now in GitHub Copilot — Sources: Hacker News, Techmeme
  • Banks tell customers AI agent risk is theirs — Sources: TechCrunch
  • Wellington IT hack exposes Irish credit union data — Sources: BleepingComputer

item.title: Java4Shell Java flaw, GPT-6.2 launch, Docker Hub key theft
item.description:
A critical Java flaw called Java4Shell affects Jenkins, Jira and other major applications, and Oracle has patched it. OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, and researchers show cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images are stolen within seconds. Also: the Microsoft 365 outage, a Fugaku supercomputer breach, a Gemini agent test and an FAA router pause.

Stories covered:

  • Critical Java4Shell flaw hits major Java applications — Sources: BleepingComputer, Techmeme, Hacker News
  • OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol — Sources: OpenAI, GitHub Changelog, Techmeme
  • Cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images stolen in seconds — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Microsoft 365 outage spread as failover shifted traffic — Sources: Techmeme, Techmeme, The Register Security
  • Fugaku supercomputer taken offline after cyberattack — Sources: BleepingComputer, The Register Security
  • Gemini agents tried to hack in safety test — Sources: The Register Security, TechCrunch
  • FAA pauses Juniper router installs after ground stop — Sources: Techmeme

item.title: Optimizely supply chain attack, AI-built exploits, Project Zero
item.description:
A supply chain attack on Optimizely put malicious scripts on well-known websites, and Google reports an AI agent that turned patches into exploits without human help. Also: Project Zero shortens its disclosure deadlines, the Barracuda and Uber breaches, California's lawsuit against OpenAI, and Microsoft's explanation of its email outage.

Stories covered:

  • Optimizely supply chain attack hits major brand sites — Sources: BleepingComputer, Techmeme
  • Google: AI agent turned patches into working exploits — Sources: The Register Security, The Next Web
  • Project Zero shortens bug disclosure deadlines — Sources: BleepingComputer, Dark Reading, The Next Web, Techmeme
  • Barracuda breach tied to ARTEX AI framework — Sources: BleepingComputer, TechCrunch, The Register Security
  • Uber says Fireworks AI breach exposed driver licenses — Sources: TechCrunch
  • California sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents — Sources: TechCrunch, The Record, BleepingComputer, Techmeme, BleepingComputer
  • Microsoft blames 365 outage on July software defect — Sources: Hacker News, The Next Web, Ars Technica, The Register

item.title: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns, Cursor extension attack, FBI warns of ARTEX
item.description:
Today's brief covers Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO, the Cursor and Fireworks A I incident behind a tampered Claude Code extension, and an F B I warning about the ARTEX attack framework. It also covers an A W S sign-in outage in US East one and a data breach at France's Maileva.

Stories covered:

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid spy scandal — Sources: The Verge AI, The Verge
  • Stolen key led to tampered Claude Code extension in Cursor — Sources: The Hacker News
  • FBI warns ARTEX A I tool is automating cyberattacks — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • AWS sign-in and connectivity errors in US-EAST-1 — Sources: AWS Status
  • Cyberattack on La Poste unit exposes data of 22 million — Sources: DataBreaches.net
